subject: alg-diagonal-adagrad-online-regret

independent_counterexample.data: d=1,C=[0,1],x1=0,ell1(x)=-sqrt(x),eta>0,epsilon>0 arbitrary. Closed nonempty convex C and finite convex loss satisfy original inputs.
independent_counterexample.convexity: For0<=a<=1 andx,y>=0, ((1-a)sqrt(x)+a sqrt(y))^2=(1-a)x+ay-a(1-a)(sqrt(x)-sqrt(y))^2 <=(1-a)x+ay. Monotonicity of nonnegative square root proves concavity of sqrt and hence convexity of its negative, including zero endpoint.
independent_counterexample.empty_subdifferential: A finite scalar g in partial ell1(0) would require -sqrt(y)>=gy, hence g<=-1/sqrt(y), for every0<y<=1. For any finiteg choose y=1/[4(|g|+1)^2] in(0,1]; then -1/sqrt(y)=-2(|g|+1)<g, contradiction.
independent_counterexample.consequence: No first gradient can be chosen; epsilon regularization and unique quadratic minimizer cannot repair a missing vector input. This refutes unconditional per-round definition, not the conditional regret theorem.

recommended_repair: Treat a finite valid subgradient as supplied round input and explicitly require its availability at every queried iterate; qualify the finite-round well-definedness claim by those inputs. This preserves arbitrary closed convex feasible sets, arbitrary nonsmooth convex losses when valid queried subgradients are supplied, every valid update and all existing regret constants.
scope_preserved: All accumulator/update formulas and positive epsilon/eta conventions
All finite valid subgradient sequences, including zero gradients and singleton/unbounded C where admissible
Generic arbitrary-vector subproblem and one-step bounds
Conditional regret theorem Statement and all proof steps
No unnecessary global smoothness, ambient open extension, differentiability or global subdifferential nonemptiness imposed
No new failure status or numeric solver guarantee invented

guarded_future_source_operations.before:
Let d>=1 and let C be a nonempty closed convex subset of R^d, closed in the standard Euclidean metric topology of [[lem-metrics-on-rn]] and convex as in [[def-convex-subset-of-euclidean-space]]. Fix x_1 in C, a constant eta>0, and epsilon>0. On round t, after observing a convex loss ell_t:C->R, choose a subgradient g_t in partial ell_t(x_t), with subgradient convention [[def-subgradient-and-subdifferential]]. For j=1,...,d set

$$s_{t,j}=\sqrt{\epsilon^2+\sum_{k=1}^t g_{k,j}^2},\qquad A_t=\operatorname{diag}(s_{t,1},...,s_{t,d}).$$

For a positive diagonal matrix A, write ||z||_A^2=z^TAz. Set x_{t+1} to the unique minimizer

$$x_{t+1}=\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in C}\{\eta\langle g_t,x\rangle+\tfrac12\|x-x_t\|_{A_t}^2\}.$$

Because epsilon>0, every diagonal entry s_{t,j} is positive. The displayed minimizer exists and is unique by [[lem-diagonal-adagrad-subproblem-well-defined]], so the procedure is defined at each finite round. This is the proximal update in the diagonal metric A_t; after the coordinate scaling A_t^{1/2}, its subproblem is an ordinary Euclidean proximal problem in the sense of [[def-proximal-mapping]].
